title: DEVELOPMENT OF ON-ORBIT MANUFACTURING PROCESS FOR LARGE ANTENNA REFLECTOR - EXPRO PLUS
description: To select, develop and demonstrate on a breadboard a process relevant for on-orbit manufacturingof large antenna reflectors.DescriptionThe size of the Telecommunication satellites is limited by the dimensions of the launcher fairings.This applies to components of the satellites where a larger size results in increased performance and capability of the system. Larger solar arrays result in more power available for a given platform and increased payload capability. Larger antenna reflectors lead to a smaller emitted beam and therefore higher gain, higher data throughput and the ability to divide the available power between an increased number of smaller beams. Current solutions for large reflectors rely on deployablesystems, which have highly complex manufacturing and testing routes, which result in long lead times and high cost. The ability to manufacture antenna reflectors and booms on orbit allows to alleviate the limitation of the fairing size and the impact of the launch vibrations, thereby enabling very large size antennae and improved system performance. Manufacturing and assemblyprocesses for on-orbit manufacturing have been proposed and tested on ground by several actors,including in Europe. The first in orbit demonstration missions for in-situ manufacturing and assemblyof spacecraft components are scheduled in the U.S. before 2025.This activity proposes to select, develop and demonstrate a process relevant to future on-orbitmanufacturing of large antenna reflectors. The process to be developed could be an on-orbit manufacturing technique,to produce antenna structural components (e.g. antenna frame structural beam, boom, reflective surface elements) or an on-orbit assembly technique, to join structural components together (e.g. joining of reflector membrane on the antenna structure frame). The emphasis will be put on continuous or semi-continuous processes (over batch processes). This, inorder to address antenna concepts involving large structural elements (e.g. large mesh or trussstructure), as opposed to concepts relying on assembly of a high number of small constitutive elements, which have been explored in previous activities.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Reviewof use cases for very large antenna reflectors- Review of existing and potential solutions for on-orbit manufacturing and assemblyof large antenna reflector structural elements (composites, polymers, metals, ceramics)- Definition of requirements for the manufacturing method- Trade-off and selection of manufacturing method to be developed- Manufacturing and characterization of small-scalespecimens- Design and manufacturing of a breadboard and demonstration of elemental performance requirements- Development plan towards on-orbit demonstration.

description: University of Helsinki, on behalf and representing the FLEX-EPOS national consortium of universities and research institutes will carry out a purchase of seismic instruments in 2020-2024. The FLEX-EPOS consortium is chaired by the University of Helsinki (UH), Department of Geosciences and Geography, and the other consortium members are as follows: University of Oulu, Faculty of Technology, Oulu Mining School (OMS), Geological Survey of Finland (GTK), University of Turku (UTU), Aalto University (AU), Finnish Geospatial Research Institute (FGI) of the National Land Survey, and VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland Ltd. The consortium will build a national pool of geophysical instruments and multidisciplinary geophysical superstations in seismology, geomagnetism and geodesy. The present tender is about Broadband instrumentation for seismic observations. The present tender is about Broadband instrumentation for seismic observations. The tender is for 30 instruments, with an option to purchase 0-30 more, i.e., altogether up to 60 instruments. Each broadband instrument for seismic observations should consist of a digitizer and a separate three-component sensor pair, and must come with required cabling for full operation, including external GNSS antenna and open-ended cable for external DC power. System must support surface installations. System must be operable with a single power cable. Specifically, the sensor must be powered without an additional power cable. System must provide a SEED-link server, usable through Ethernet for data access. System must be configurable through an Ethernet connection in situ using an off-the-shelf laptop without access to Internet and without any special software. The computer can be expected to have standard software, such as an SSH-client and an Internet browser. Data stored in internal memory must be accessible in miniSEED format. Digitizer must also support hot-swappable external memory storage card of at least 64 GB, i.e. data can be collected by changing the memory storage card in the field on the fly without interruption to data collection. System must support automatic calibration and centering of the sensor. The offered package should include all necessary hardware and software for full operation. The Seller must take full responsibility for the functioning system of the delivered equipment.

title: LARGE UNFURLABLE REFLECTOR SURFACE ASSEMBLY FOR KA-BAND APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 5B.169) ( RE-ISSUE OF ITT 1-8909)
description: Objective of the activity is to design, develop and verify an unfurlable reflector surface assembly suitable for use in large European antennas operating in the 20 - 35 GHz frequency range.Targeted Improvements: Enabling technology development for a new source of unfurlable reflectors capable of generating the high gain, narrow beams needed in terabit/s high throughput satellite systems.Description: The next generation of high throughput satellites (HTS) that are intended to reach terabit/s capacity requirehighly directive antennas and hence large radiating apertures with diameters ranging from 3.5 to 5 metres at Ka-band. Due to the accommodation constraints of the launcher fairing, only antennas with deployable apertures can meet this need. Large antennas with unfurlable reflectors have attracted significant interest in Europe in recent years as critical technology for European non-dependence.Reflector antennas of the 5 metre class operating at Ka-band will be a key enabler for the next generation of HTS. However, today areflective surface that can be stowed and unfurled without compromising the surface accuracy and thermal stability is not available.In this activity a large unfurlable reflector surface assembly shall be designed and developed with adequate RF and mechanical properties for Ka-band applications. Investigations shall include promising solutions, such as metallic mesh or carbon fibre reinforcedsilicone (CFRS) for the RF reflective surface, as well as a suitable support structure, such as a carrying net made of tensioning ties. A prototype of large reflector surface assembly shall be manufactured. The built prototype shall then be tested, including verification of thedeployment, surface accuracy, RF and passive intermodulation performance. Limitations and improvements to utilize the technology forantenna diameters up to 8m shall be identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to EMITS news "Industrial Policy measures for non-primes, SMEs and RD entities in ESA programmes".
